candidateVerificationJourney.restrictedRoute: Contract tests on feature/issue-751; the script itself is exercised only on the next real deploy

journeys.name: deploy-restarts-celery-units
assertions: deploy-release.sh restarts juli-celery-worker and juli-celery-beat in addition to juli-api and juli-web
the restart happens after the current symlink is flipped, so workers load the new release
a host without the Celery units installed does not fail the deploy
juli-api and juli-web restart behaviour is unchanged

migrationCompatibility.notes: No schema change. This edits the deploy shell script only; the alembic revision graph is untouched.

rollbackAssertion.preCutoverFailureBehavior: Do not merge. Deploys continue to leave Celery workers on the previous release, requiring a manual systemctl restart after every worker-code deploy — the current state, no regression.
rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: Revert the script change. Reverting restores the manual-restart status quo and cannot leave services stopped, because the added restarts are additive and guarded by a unit-existence check. If a restart itself fails mid-deploy, juli-api and juli-web have already restarted and the operator can restart the Celery units by hand.

acceptanceCommands: python -m pytest tests/unit -q -k 'deploy or release_script or celery'
doNotInfer: this health-checks the Celery workers after restart — the script health-checks only the HTTP surface, and worker health remains unverified
this changes the systemd units themselves — only deploy-release.sh is edited
the first deploy after this merges will pick up worker code automatically without verification — confirm via /proc/<pid>/cwd that workers loaded the new release
this addresses the hour-granular reconcile dedup that makes manual test runs appear to do nothing
